key_insight: A quantum generator with a fixed circuit and a trained linear output layer can remain competitive without entangling gates, while avoiding circuit-training barren plateaus.
engineering_relevance: For the tested generation tasks, simpler quantum reservoirs may reduce circuit demands without sacrificing performance.
method: Encode random latent vectors into quantum states, apply a fixed unitary, and measure features.
Train only a linear output layer using expectation values or single-measurement outputs.
Use Pauli propagation to analyze how Clifford, T-doped, and Haar-random circuits transform encoding-defined functions.
evidence_signal: Tests on one- and two-dimensional distributions found no systematic improvement from Clifford-generated entanglement or Haar-random reservoir nonstabilizerness; a gate-free reservoir was competitive.
watch_item: Findings are limited to the proposed encoding and tested distributions; deeper Haar-random circuits also reduced feature variation with the latent input.
